newsitem.title: BELARUS: Chernomyrdin optimistic on Belarus solution.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin optimistic on Belarus solution.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, mediating in a standoff between opposing political forces in Belarus, indicated on Friday he was optimistic a solution could be found.
Arriving with a smiling President Alexander Lukashenko at talks with Lukashenko's parliamentary rivals, Chernomrydin gave reporters a thumbs up sign. "We are in a good mood," he said.
Earlier Belarus parliamentary leader Semyon Sharetsky held talks with Russian counterparts and said that he was "very happy" with the results of the meeting.

Gennady Seleznyov, leader of Russia's lower house of parliament, said they had several offers to put on the table at the talks with Lukashenko, who has called a controversial referendum for Sunday on extending his powers.

"We have several compromise options which would lead to a "zero" (option)," Seleznyov said. The Belarus parliament has started impeachment proceedings against Lukashenko but indicated it might drop them if he compromises over the referendum.

Interfax news agency quoted sources at the earlier Lukashenko-Chermomyrdin talks as saying they had reached a separate compromise under which the referendum could still go ahead. The two sides later started talks on a solution at Lukashenko's meeting house in central Minsk.
